messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High-severity — autoscaler failing to add GPU capacity in gcp-us-central1. Queue growth on inference frontends > 2000, token latency spiking. Paging on-call now.
vikas: on it. seeing autoscaler errors in the controller logs: 'QuotaExceeded: QUOTA  GPUs per region exceeded for project'. starting triage — attaching first pass logs.
maya: noticed increased 95/99p on conversational endpoints, some requests timing out after 30s. Affects both hosted and a few dedicated pools pinned to the region.
david: collecting autoscaler events. looks like the cluster requested new nodes but GCP returned 403/QUOTA for GPUs. autoscaler retried and backed off. queued pods staying Pending because no GPU resources available.
lia: customer-facing: we have two paying customers reporting elevated tail latency. opening support incidents and prepping a public status note if we have >30m impact.
ops-bot: deploy-log: started attempt to spin up fallback cpu-only workers in us-central1 at 3104567955 — some traffic diverted but model quality/timeouts expected for large-gen workloads.
vikas: mitigation options brainstorm:
- route new traffic to eu-west1/us-west2 (have spare GPU capacity there)
- spin up preemptible GPUs in other projects/regions
- reduce per-request concurrency and apply per-customer throttles
- warm a smaller quantized model on CPU as a temporary fallback
- request quota increase with GCP (slow)
maya: prioritise routing and per-customer throttles. quality team ok with routing for non-SLA customers. for SLAs we must keep latency target — may need dedicated reserved capacity in a different region.
david: command I'll run to force routing change (will affect canary + 10% traffic):
```
POST /admin/routing/override
{ "match": {"route":"/v1/generate"}, "target":"us-west2", "weight": 0.1 }
```
I'll also scale down non-critical batch jobs in us-central1: `kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/batch-render` to free up CPUs/GPU attach operations.
vikas: ran `gcloud compute region-quotas describe --project=myproj --region=us-central1` -> shows GPUs: limit 100, usage 100, pending 0. So hard cap. Need quota increase request but approval ETA hours-days.
lia: support note draft: "We're currently experiencing increased latencies for inference in us-central1 due to exhausted GPU quota. We are diverting traffic and throttling to limit customer impact. We will post updates every 15 minutes." Suggestions?
support-eng: add PSAT for customers on Dedicated — they need to know if failover will route outside their allowed regions.
maya: good call. for Dedicated customers with region lock we need to offer either a temporary CPU fallback or contact their account team for emergency reserved pool in allowed region.
incident-bot: New action: @vikas to coordinate cross-region routing; @david to free up local capacity; @lia to publish support notice; @maya to verify model fallbacks. ETA 15m for first mitigation.
vikas: started traffic shift: increased weight to us-west2 0.25 at 3104568030. monitoring queue size... queue growth rate dropped ~35%.
david: freed ~12 GPU attach slots by scaling down noncritical deployments and deleting 3 stale node-pools. logs show pending pods decrementing slowly.
ops-bot: metric alert suppressed for 10m to avoid noisy paging while mitigation runs.
lia: posted support update at 3104568060. snippet: "We've detected GPU quota limits in gcp-us-central1 causing delayed requests. Traffic routing changes underway; minor degraded performance for some customers. Next update 15m."
maya: QA: routed traffic shows 99p tail latency still elevated for large-context jobs (some still pinned to us-central1 due to customer region restrictions). for those, enabling CPU fallback reduces failures but increases response time and occasionally truncates outputs.
support-eng: compiling list of impacted customers with SLA flags. sending to account teams now.
vikas: next steps: 1) escalate to cloud ops to request emergency quota bump (ticket created) 2) provision dedicated reserved pool in us-west2 for 24h 3) continue routing shift for non-SLA customers 4) document temporary throttles applied per-customer.
david: running final check on autoscaler: patching autoscaler backoff to be more aggressive on cross-region fallback (experimental) — pushing hotfix to canary in us-west2 only.
lia: customer comms ready for escalation if we cross 30m degraded window. will include mitigation summary and ETA for resolution.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Traffic diversion reduced queue growth. Some SLAs still impacted. Current status: mitigation in progress. Next update in 15m.
vikas: leaving note for on-call handoff in 30m: if quota bump not approved, escalate to SRE lead + sales for contract-level mitigation. handing over to david for next 30m.
david: ack, taking over. I'll monitor queue, autoscaler, and routing. if queue > 3000 or >10% retries, we'll trigger failover to multi-region read-only endpoints.
maya: capturing evals for quality regression on CPU fallback so we can revert if outputs unacceptable.
lia: support: continuing ticket updates. prepared FAQ for customers who ask about region failover and data residency.
pagerduty-bot: Handoff: rotation=nightops, assignee=david, runbook_link=https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu_quota_failures at 3104568123
